/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 1

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 1](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G` the maximum number of leaves of a spanning
tree satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ n(G) + 1 - 2·m(G)` where `n(G)` counts vertices and
`m(G)` is the size of a maximum matching.

A formal proof reduces to a spanning tree `T`. If `I` is the set of non-leaves
of `T`, Hall's theorem applied to a bipartition of `T` gives a matching `M`
with `|I| + 1 ≤ 2 * |M|`. Since `|V|` is the sum of the numbers of leaves and
non-leaves, and every matching and leaf count constructed in `T` is admissible
for the corresponding supremum in `G`, the stated inequality follows.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/MiskinAleksandr23/WOWII-1/blob/eda16f6e96b313bd112351ae9859133b77d537c9/WOWII1/GraphConjecture1.lean"]
theorem conjecture1 {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    (Fintype.card α : ℝ) + 1 - 2 * matchingNumber G ≤ (Ls G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

review.notes:
I found no misformalizations and no status issues.

Checks done:
(1) I read the source's definitions. L_s(G) is the maximum number of degree-one vertices in the spanning tree, over all spanning trees. μ(G) is the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. n is the number of vertices. These match `Ls`, `matchingNumber` and `Fintype.card α`. Both `sSup`s are over non-empty, bounded sets in the reachable domain. For `Ls`, a connected graph with n ≥ 2 has a spanning tree. For `matchingNumber`, `⊥` is a matching. So each value is the true maximum. The junk value `Ls = 0` for disconnected graphs cannot be reached because of `h_conn`.
(2) The inequality is stated in ℝ, so truncated subtraction plays no role. The parse is `((n + 1) - 2μ) ≤ Ls`.
(3) `[Nontrivial α]` is an extra hypothesis compared with the source's headline ('If G is a simple connected graph'). It is necessary and justified. In a scratch file I proved that the statement fails for the one-vertex graph on `Fin 1`: matchingNumber ≤ 0 and Ls ≤ 0, so 2 ≤ 0 would be needed. Under any convention L_s(K1) ≤ 1 < 2. The source's own comment restricts the proven result to 'connected graphs on at least two vertices'. So the Lean states the claim as the source records it.
(4) The category `research solved` matches the source's status 'T' (Fajtlowicz 1996). The `formal_proof` link points to an external file that proves the identical signature with the same repository definitions and contains no `sorry`. I did not compile it.

Small documentation nit, not reported as a finding: the theorem docstring says 'For a simple connected graph G' and does not mention the n ≥ 2 restriction that the Lean imposes. AGENTS.md asks for such restrictions to be explained. Adding 'on at least two vertices' (per the source comment) would align the docstring with the Lean.
